mnemonic: A mouth 口 in the gateway 門 putting the question formally, and this one is not asking anybody's age: とう.
notes: 聞く きく asks in the ordinary way and 尋ねる たずねる goes looking for the answer. 問う is formal, often written, and often negative: 年齢は問わない.
sentence: 応募者の年齢は問いません。
sentence_meaning: We will not inquire about the age of the applicants.

mnemonic: The heart 心 in a tangle, which is the falling sort rather than the settled sort, and it is showing on her face: こい.
notes: 愛 あい is love as something steady you carry about, and 大好き だいすき is loving a thing casually. 恋 is falling for somebody, and it is the 恋 in 恋人.
sentence: 彼女は恋をしてきれいになったね。
sentence_meaning: She fell in love and became beautiful.

mnemonic: Going home in the middle of a shift with the work still out on the desk. Not merely wrong, out of the question: とんでもない.
sentence: 仕事中に帰るなんてとんでもない。
sentence_meaning: It's unthinkable to go home in the middle of work.

mnemonic: The middle 中 and the heart 心 of it, which is the point every other part is arranged around. Stand just here: ちゅうしん.
notes: 中央 ちゅうおう is the centre as a spot on a map. 中心 is the centre as the core of a thing, and it does figurative work as well.
sentence: ここが建物の中心です。
sentence_meaning: This is the center of the building.

mnemonic: Water 氵 of the sort that comes out of you rather than out of a tap, and it was standing on his forehead: あせ.
sentence: 彼は額に汗をかいていたの。
sentence_meaning: He was sweating from his forehead.

mnemonic: Different 異 from what is usually 常 the case, and this summer has gone a long way past it: いじょう.
notes: Same reading as 以上 いじょう, or more. 異常 is abnormal, and 非常 ひじょう is the emergency one.
sentence: 今年の夏は異常な暑さですね。
sentence_meaning: This summer is exceptionally hot.

mnemonic: Not 非 the usual 常 state of affairs, said of the sort of situation that comes with its own exits: ひじょう.
notes: Also does very, as 非常に. 異常 いじょう is the near neighbour and means abnormal.
sentence: 非常事態です。
sentence_meaning: We're in a state of emergency!

mnemonic: The flesh 月 joint that meets the ground before any other part of you does, and skiing found it: ひざ.
sentence: スキーで膝を怪我しました。
sentence_meaning: I injured my knee while skiing.

mnemonic: A savings book with almost nothing in it, and that is what he is living on. Less a small amount than barely any: わずか.
notes: 少ない すくない is simply not many. わずか leans on how little there is, and usually on it not being enough.
sentence: 彼はわずかな貯金で暮らしている。
sentence_meaning: He lives on his meager savings.

mnemonic: The part you are handed and then walk out to go and do, and he gets the detective more often than not: やく.
notes: 一部 いちぶ and 部分 ぶぶん are a part of something. 役 is a part you play.
sentence: 彼はよく刑事の役を演じるね。
sentence_meaning: He often plays the part of a detective.

meaning: to feel pressured, to feel hurried
mnemonic: A bird 隹 held over the fire 灬 and beginning to catch, which is what being rushed feels like from the inside. What is the hurry: あせる.
notes: One kana from 汗 あせ, sweat, and the two turn up together often enough to be worth noticing.
sentence: 何をそんなに焦っているのですか。
sentence_meaning: What are you in such a hurry for?

mnemonic: Two banks with the water running down between them, seen from above and no more complicated than that. A small one to cross: かわ.
notes: 河 is the same reading for a larger river. 川 is the everyday word and the one in place names.
sentence: 小さな川を渡りました。
sentence_meaning: I crossed a small river.

mnemonic: Bad 悪 with the magic 魔 turned the whole way up, and he is not far off it himself: あくま.
sentence: 彼はまるで悪魔みたいな男だ。
sentence_meaning: He's almost like a demon.

mnemonic: One 一 bird 隹 and one mouth 口 and nothing else anywhere in the frame. Fishing is the whole of what he enjoys: ゆいいつ.
sentence: 彼の唯一の楽しみは釣りです。
sentence_meaning: His sole pleasure is fishing.

mnemonic: Half eleven, and the part of the morning where nobody starts anything new. It is nearly lunch: もうすぐ.
notes: そろそろ is soon in the sense that it is about time to move. もうすぐ is soon on the clock.
sentence: 今11時半。もうすぐランチの時間です。
sentence_meaning: It's almost 11:30. It will be lunch time soon.

mnemonic: Middle 中 and middle 央 again, both halves saying the same thing, which is how you get the centre of a town on a map: ちゅうおう.
notes: 中心 ちゅうしん is the core of a thing and works figuratively. 中央 is a place, and it turns up in station and street names.
sentence: その公園は町のほぼ中央に位置するんだ。
sentence_meaning: That park is located almost in the center of town.

meaning: to thrust in, to dash into
mnemonic: You drive 突 the thing in 込 without once looking at what you are doing, and the wallet is now somewhere in that pocket: つっこむ.
sentence: ポケットに財布を突っ込んじゃった。
sentence_meaning: I thrust my wallet into my pocket.

mnemonic: Skill in the hand 技 and a learned way of going about it 術, which between them is what a company has to sell: ぎじゅつ.
sentence: この会社にはどんな技術がありますか。
sentence_meaning: What kind of technology does this company have?

mnemonic: Plain 素 clear sky 晴 with nothing at all in the way of it, and the chance in front of you is the same: すばらしい.
notes: 見事 みごと and 立派 りっぱ both admire something that was done. 素晴らしい is broader and warmer than either.
sentence: これは素晴らしいチャンスだ。
sentence_meaning: This is a great chance.

mnemonic: One 単 thread with nothing else spun into it 純, which about a person is a compliment and an observation at the same time: たんじゅん.
notes: 簡単 かんたん is simple as in easy to do and ただ is simply as in merely. 単純 is simple as in not complicated, and about a person it can be pointed.
sentence: 彼は単純な人です。
sentence_meaning: He's a simple person.

mnemonic: The grain 禾 is in and everything has settled behind it, with nothing about the year going wrong. That is the life they have: おだやか.
notes: 冷静 れいせい is keeping your head under pressure. 穏やか is weather, sea or a life with nothing rough anywhere in it.
sentence: 彼らは穏やかな暮らしをしているの。
sentence_meaning: They live a quiet life.

mnemonic: The whole weight of the thing comes down 撃 at once and from a distance away. He was hit with a handgun: うつ.
notes: Same reading as 打つ うつ, striking a thing with your own hand. 撃つ is firing a weapon, and 放つ はなつ is letting the shot go. 火 ひ is the other fire, the noun.
sentence: 彼は拳銃で撃たれたわ。
sentence_meaning: He was shot with a handgun.

mnemonic: The hand 扌 goes down and closes 合 round something that was not yours a second earlier. A wallet, in the street: ひろう.
notes: 見つける みつける is spotting a thing. 拾う is bending down and picking it up.
sentence: 道で財布を拾った。
sentence_meaning: I picked up a wallet in the street.

mnemonic: Finished 完 and carried all the way there 成, both halves saying so. The new site went live this morning: かんせい.
sentence: 新しいホームページが完成した。
sentence_meaning: Our new home page is completed.

mnemonic: The plant in the hedge you were warned about as a child, and the fourth drink is doing the same job: どく.
sentence: 飲みすぎは体に毒ですよ。
sentence_meaning: Drinking too much is poison to your body.

mnemonic: The one animal in the deck you could pick out of its own character across a field. He wants to go and see one: うま.
sentence: 馬を見たいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to see a horse.

mnemonic: A lid comes over the top and now you cannot see anything that is under it. The entire sky has gone that way: おおう.
notes: 隠す かくす is hiding a thing so that it will not be found. 覆う is putting something over the top of it.
sentence: 雲が空を覆っているね。
sentence_meaning: Clouds are covering the sky.

mnemonic: What you run 走 to take up 取 and have a taste 味 for. Mine is karaoke, since you ask: しゅみ.
sentence: 趣味はカラオケです。
sentence_meaning: My hobby is karaoke.

mnemonic: The deadline was going to go and then it did not, and nobody could tell you exactly how. It got there: どうにか.
notes: 何とか なんとか is the near twin and often interchangeable. 何だか なんだか is a different word, somehow as in for some reason, and so are どうも and どうか, which is a plea.
sentence: どうにか締め切りに間に合った。
sentence_meaning: I somehow managed to meet the deadline.

mnemonic: Nothing is wrong with the party and nobody has upset you, and you would still rather not go: なんとなく.
notes: 何だか なんだか and どうも do much the same job. 何となく leans on there being no reason you could name.
sentence: パーティーに行くのは何となく気が進まないな。
sentence_meaning: For some reason I don't feel like going to the party.

mnemonic: What a person 亻 reckons it is worth looking at it straight 直, which is not the same as the price on the label. That was worth hearing: かち.
sentence: とても価値のある話を聞いたよ。
sentence_meaning: I heard a very valuable story.

meaning: to watch, to keep watch over
mnemonic: You watch 見 and you guard 守 and you do not step in. All of us, warmly, from over here: みまもる.
sentence: 皆で暖かく見守りましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's all warmly watch over them.

mnemonic: Peaceful 安 and whole 全, which is precisely what you want everybody going home as. That, before anything else: あんぜん.
sentence: 安全が第一です。
sentence_meaning: Safety comes first.

meaning: to bring over, to bring along
mnemonic: You take somebody along 連 and come 来 back with them still attached. His friend, all the way to the house: つれてくる.
notes: 連れて行く つれていく is the same trip in the other direction, away from where you are.
sentence: 弟が家へ友達を連れてきました。
sentence_meaning: My younger brother brought home his friend.

mnemonic: Near enough to touch and staying there, which is the whole of what is being asked. Do not go anywhere: そば.
notes: Also the noodles, written 蕎麦, which is a separate word that happens to sound the same.
sentence: そばにいてください。
sentence_meaning: Stay with me.

mnemonic: Four digits and then this character takes over, so ten thousand is 一万. Those shoes are one of them: まん.
notes: Japanese counts in units of 10,000: 一万 is ten thousand and 十万 is a hundred thousand, so the groupings fall differently from English.
sentence: この靴は1万円です。
sentence_meaning: These shoes are ten thousand yen.

mnemonic: A frame is a guest's 客 face 頁 hung up on the wall, and the photograph went into one: がく.
notes: Read ひたい the same character is your forehead, which is the 額 in 額に汗. がく is the frame, and also a sum of money.
sentence: 写真を額に入れて飾ったんだ。
sentence_meaning: I put the photo in a frame and hung it up.

mnemonic: You take it 受 and you stop it 止 dead, both in the one movement. That one came in far too fast: うけとめる.
notes: もらう is receiving something you were given. 受け止める is stopping something that was coming at you.
sentence: ボールが速すぎて受け止められなかったの。
sentence_meaning: The ball was so fast that I couldn't catch it.

mnemonic: The two characters were borrowed for their sound and do not add up to the meaning at all. What they say about the shirt is that it is lovely: すてき.
notes: The characters are ateji, picked for sound rather than sense, so there is nothing to read out of them.
sentence: かっこいいシャツですね。素敵です。
sentence_meaning: That is a cool shirt. It looks great.

mnemonic: The correct 正 body 体 underneath whatever has been laid over the top of it. Next week they find out who he is: しょうたい.
sentence: 次回、謎の人物の正体が明かされる。
sentence_meaning: Next time, the identity of the mysterious person will be revealed.

mnemonic: Said in one breath and moved straight past, as though it had cost nothing at all to say. Not with this one: あっさり.
notes: Also used of food, where it means light and not rich, the opposite of こってり. ただ is simply as in merely.
sentence: そうあっさり言わないで。
sentence_meaning: Don't say it so lightly.

mnemonic: A mouth 口 drawing something inward rather than letting it back out, and here it is a cigarette. Not in this room: すう.
notes: The same verb does breathing in, 息を吸う. With タバコ it is smoking.
sentence: ここでタバコを吸わないでください。
sentence_meaning: Please don't smoke here.

mnemonic: A bird's 鳥 mouth 口 going off in the quiet, except that it is your phone and the whole carriage is looking: なる.
notes: Same reading as なる, to become, which is written in kana. 鳴る is a sound going off, and 鳴く なく is an animal making one.
sentence: 携帯が大きな音で鳴っています。
sentence_meaning: The cell phone is ringing loudly.

mnemonic: Grind 研 away at the thing and then go all the way down to the bottom of it 究, for years on end. Maths, at graduate school: けんきゅう.
sentence: 大学院で数学を研究したいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to do mathematics research in grad school.

meaning: to gather together, to put in order
mnemonic: Everything that was spread across two rooms is in one bag by the door, and she is going: まとめる.
sentence: 彼女は荷物をまとめて出て行った。
sentence_meaning: She packed her baggage and left.

mnemonic: Two people who came to the station together walk out of it separately 別, and neither of them is upset about it: わかれる.
notes: 分かれる わかれる is the same reading for a thing splitting in two, a road or an opinion. 別れる is people parting.
sentence: 駅で友だちと別れました。
sentence_meaning: I parted with my friend at the station.

meaning: to mess around, to fool around
mnemonic: Somebody is not taking a word of this seriously and the room has stopped finding it funny. Pack it in: ふざける.
sentence: ふざけるのは止めて。
sentence_meaning: Stop messing around.

mnemonic: What you have on 着 gets swapped 替 for something else, and the clean shirt wins: きがえる.
sentence: 彼はきれいな服に着替えた。
sentence_meaning: He changed into clean clothes.

mnemonic: Bamboo 竹 slats set against one another 相 to make six sides and a lid. This one takes two people to shift: はこ.
sentence: この箱は重い。
sentence_meaning: This box is heavy.

mnemonic: No 無 speech 言 at all, not once, for an entire day, and every person in the office noticed: むごん.
sentence: 彼は一日中無言だったな。
sentence_meaning: He was silent all day long.
